review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] declarations and no local simp sets, and most simp use is `simpa`. I searched the ChipFiringWithLean, Foundations and Gluing directories for existing degree and chip lemmas. `deg_one_chip` is already @[simp]. I found no problem worth reporting in the `bnRank` or `BNRankGe` simp interface. The `norm_num; exact hDegree` step in `exists_chip_pair_of_effective_deg_two` is fragile but minor. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether the proposed lemma would turn each `simpa` into a plain `simp`. I am also unsure whether `deg_zsmul_one_chip` in Gluing/GenusTwoTwoPole.lean can be imported from here without a cycle.

findings.problem: There is no canonical simp lemma for the degree of a repeated chip, `CFDiv.degree (n • oneChip v) = n`. Only `deg_one_chip` is @[simp]. Each time the file needs the degree of `m.toNat • oneChip v`, it unfolds the `let` with `dsimp` and calls `simpa [Int.toNat_of_nonneg _] using (AddMonoidHom.map_nsmul CFDiv.degree _ (oneChip v))`. This happens three times here, at lines 120-123, 201-204 and 226-229. The same block is copied in RankInvariance.lean (about line 77) and ElementaryExistence.lean (lines 38 and 77), and Rank.lean line 74 has a variant. `deg_zsmul_one_chip` in Gluing/GenusTwoTwoPole.lean covers the ℤ-smul form, but it is not simp. So simp has no rule for the normal form of `degree (n • oneChip v)`, and every proof supplies the `map_nsmul` term by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas next to `deg_one_chip` in ChipFiringWithLean/Basic.lean. One would be `CFDiv.degree (n • oneChip v) = n` for `n : ℕ`, with the cast on the right. The other would be the ℤ-smul version, which is `deg_zsmul_one_chip` promoted to @[simp]. Add a further lemma for `(m.toNat) • oneChip v` under `0 ≤ m`, with the hypothesis dischargeable by `omega` or `hr`. Then each of the three blocks becomes `by simp [E, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hr]` or a single `rw`. The `AddMonoidHom.map_nsmul` term is no longer needed.
findings.benefit: A single oriented rule fixes the normal form of degrees of piles of chips. It removes about a dozen copies of the same four-line proof across the Foundations files. Later proofs about piles of chips can then call `simp` instead of re-deriving the degree each time.
